edge.title: The flat that doesn't exist
edge.anchor: A Bengaluru woman lost ₹21 lakh to an online property enquiry — reported in this week's city pages.
edge.setup: You find a 2BHK listed well under market rate. The "owner" is warm, shares photos, an Aadhaar copy, even a video walkthrough. He's posted abroad, so a caretaker will hand over keys. He just needs the token advance today because three others are interested. Everything checks out except one thing: you have not stood inside that flat.
edge.tell: Money is moving before a key has turned in a lock you touched.
move: Never transfer anything before physically standing inside the flat with someone who can open it.
Match the name on the EC or tax receipt to the person's ID yourself — don't accept a forwarded photo.
If pressure to pay today appears, treat that as the scam announcing itself, not as competition.
edge.why: Documents are cheap to forge and free to send. Physical access is not. Every version of this scam works by substituting a convincing artefact — ID scan, video, rent agreement PDF — for the one costly thing a real owner always has: the ability to let you in.
edge.variants: Used cars "in transit from Pune" · PG deposits · plots "near the new airport" · pet sales with a transport fee.

lens.name: Induced demand
lens.one_line: Adding road capacity creates new trips that fill it, so congestion returns at a higher throughput.
lens.detail: People who had given up on a route — shifted their timing, taken transit, moved closer — return once it gets easier. The new lane doesn't serve the old traffic; it reveals suppressed demand that was always there. Measured honestly, travel time often lands back where it started within a few years, now with more vehicles.
lens.today: Academics and activists urged a rethink of the Hebbal tunnel this week, arguing it will shift chokepoints rather than remove them. That's this model, stated in civic-planning language: the tunnel doesn't reduce the number of people who want to cross Hebbal at 9am — it changes where they queue.
elsewhere: Build more parking and more people drive in.
Add engineers to a late project and the scope expands to absorb them.
Widen a hospital's OPD and the waiting room refills.
lens.test: When someone promises more capacity will fix congestion, ask: what was suppressed, and what happens when it comes back?

moved.what: Race Course Road is shut for 60 days, with diversions pushing traffic onto surrounding city-centre routes.
moved.so_what: The cost isn't the closed road — it's the two or three adjacent junctions absorbing its volume. If you cross the centre, add 20 minutes or route east of Cubbon Park entirely.

moved.what: CMRS has begun the three-day safety inspection of the Pink Line — the final regulatory step before Bengaluru's longest underground stretch opens.
moved.so_what: Inspection starting means weeks, not months. If you're flat-hunting near Jayanagar or Nagawara, this is the short window before rents price it in — today's lens, happening to you in real time.

moved.what: Cabinet approved splitting Bengaluru's single police commissionerate into five.
moved.so_what: Practical effect: the jurisdiction for filing an FIR will change. Worth knowing which commissionerate covers your address before you need it — wrong jurisdiction is the most common reason a complaint stalls on day one.

moved.what: Multiple FIRs over forged Form-7 applications — booth-level agents accused of filing bulk voter-deletion requests, 136 in a single case.
moved.so_what: Deletions don't notify you. Check your own entry on voters.eci.gov.in now; discovering it at the polling booth is too late to fix.

moved.what: Arijit Singh announced a nine-city India tour; Echoes of Earth 2026 revealed Thievery Corporation and Yussef Dayes.
moved.so_what: Both clear out in minutes on dynamically-priced platforms. The decision to make today isn't whether to go — it's whether you set a reminder for the on-sale minute, because "checking later" is the same as not going.
